units.source_excerpt: The differences between the losers and the profiteers are not only for the choice of asset variety, but also for the trading strategy.
units.function: Narrow the cause of profit from the asset to the strategy, which the paper can actually control.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the winners and the losers, then move the cause off the thing they trade and onto the decision, with 'not only ... but also'.
information_order: cause shifted to what the paper controls
reusable_elements: stable function: move the cause onto the controllable variable
slots: winners, losers, rejected cause, chosen cause
variants: the rejected cause can be the asset, the data, or the market
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: use only when the chosen cause is genuinely what the paper decides; do not use it to dismiss a cause the paper never tests

units.source_excerpt: For this purpose, we designed two models to develop our strategies: Model I: Volatile Asset Price Forecasting Model; Model II: Strategy Improvement Model.
units.function: Announce the two models as a colon list, each with a label and a job.
units.reusable_pattern: State the count, then a colon, then 'Model N: name' for each, so the label and the job arrive together.
reusable_elements: stable function: give every model a label and a job in one line
slots: count, model label, model job
variants: the list can hold two items or more
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: each item needs both a label and a job; a bare name list does not do this

units.source_excerpt: We first use the ARIMA model to forecast the price and find that it can only predict well about the linear part of bitcoin price. Second, we take the LSTM model to forecast, and just the opposite of the ARIMA model, the LSTM model is able to capture the information of the non-linear part.
units.function: Set two methods as mirrors, one taking the linear part and the other the non-linear part.
units.reusable_pattern: First method and what it captures, then 'just the opposite' and the second method with the complementary part.
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary paragraph 2, repeated in the memorandum
stable function: justify a combination by complementarity
order: method A, its scope, opposite, method B, its scope
slots: method A, method B, part A, part B
variants: the marker can be 'just the opposite' or 'on the contrary'
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: only when the two methods genuinely cover different parts; do not claim complementarity the paper does not show

units.source_excerpt: the final price prediction results almost overlap with the real results, with RMSE and MAPE were 0.0342 and 0.36, respectively.
units.function: Put the two error numbers directly after the qualitative claim so the adjective is not left bare.
units.reusable_pattern: Qualitative claim, then the metric names and the values that support it.
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary paragraph 2, confirmed by Table 1 on page 9
stable function: support an adjective with the exact numbers
variants: one number or a pair
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the numbers must be the ones computed; do not attach a number from a different model

features.quantitative_role: two error values support the claim

units.source_excerpt: After programming using MATLAB, we calculated the value of the initial money as $374,563.25 on 9/10/21 and discounted this value to five years ago to obtain $360,595.32, which means that the value of $374,563.25 on 9/10/21 is equivalent to the value of $360,595.32 on 9/10/16.
units.function: Give the dollar result, then the discounted dollar, then a 'which means' clause that ties each dollar to its date.
units.reusable_pattern: Tool clause, terminal value with its date, discounted value, then a clause restating which value belongs to which date.
reusable_elements: stable function: keep the two dollar figures from being confused
order: tool, terminal value, discounted value, which-means clause
variants: the same block is used once per model
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the which-means clause must repeat the same figures; do not introduce a third value inside it

features.quantitative_role: two dollar values tied to dates

units.source_excerpt: Again, we demonstrate that our strategy is optimal in two ways, one by changing the strategy itself and the other by observing different market environments.
units.function: Announce the number of proofs and name each, then treat them in that same order.
units.reusable_pattern: Claim, then 'in N ways, one by ... and the other by ...', followed by one block per way in the same order.
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary paragraph 5, echoed in section 7
stable function: tell the reader the shape before the detail
order: claim, count, named ways, then the ways in order
variants: two ways here, and the same frame could hold three
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the following text must actually take the ways in the announced order

features.transition: Again, one by, the other by

units.source_excerpt: Finally, we wrote a memorandum to investors detailing our modeling process, introducing our strategy, analyzing the strategy results, and informing about the risks and shortcomings of the strategy.
units.function: Close the summary by pointing at the letter and listing its contents with a run of participles.
units.reusable_pattern: Sequence word, the artifact, then four participles naming what it contains, in the order the artifact uses.
reusable_elements: stable function: end by pointing outward to the communication artifact
variants: the participle list can be shorter
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: list only contents the artifact actually has

units.source_excerpt: We created 4 genes, namely trading portfolio, trading frequency, buying strategy, and selling strategy, hoping to improve our strategy from these four dimensions.
units.function: Announce a count, name the items with 'namely', then say what the list is for.
units.reusable_pattern: We created N things, namely the list, hoping to improve the strategy along those dimensions.
reusable_elements: stable function: give a counted list and its purpose together
variants: the model announcement uses a colon list instead of namely
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the count must equal the number of items named

units.source_excerpt: In real world of finance, all buying and selling behaviors are based on people's expectations for the future, so how to predict the future price of assets as accurately as possible has become one of the most important research contents in finance.
units.function: Turn a fact about the world into the research question with a single 'so'.
units.reusable_pattern: A present-tense fact, then 'so', then the question stated as a research topic. No citation.
reusable_elements: stable function: derive the topic from a stated fact
variants: the fact can be about markets, people, or data
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the question must follow from the fact; do not use 'so' to attach an unrelated topic

units.source_excerpt: Of course, it is rogue to talk about returns without risk.
units.function: Concede the obvious objection in a blunt colloquial sentence before building on it.
units.reusable_pattern: 'Of course', then a short blunt judgment that grants the objection the reader already holds.
reusable_elements: stable function: grant the objection before answering it
variants: the judgment can be formal or colloquial
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: only for an objection the paper then answers; do not concede a flaw and leave it

units.source_excerpt: However, due to high price volatility of bitcoin, gold, which is considered as a safe-haven capital, is paired with it to form an investment portfolio.
units.function: Use 'However' to bring in the second asset as the remedy for the first asset's flaw.
units.reusable_pattern: However, the flaw of the first asset, then the second asset introduced as the hedge.
reusable_elements: stable function: introduce a second element as the fix for the first
slots: asset A, flaw, asset B
variants: the remedy can be an asset, a constraint, or a method
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the second element must actually answer the named flaw

units.source_excerpt: It is often said in finance that if investor A is a risk averter and investor B is a risk seeker, we cannot consider investor B's strategy to be superior one even if investor A's return is lower than B's return. Therefore, in this question, our strategy must be based on a given risk preference.
units.function: Set up a proverb-like example and cash it out with 'Therefore' into this paper's decision.
units.reusable_pattern: 'It is often said that' plus an example, then 'Therefore' plus what this paper must do.
reusable_elements: stable function: ground a modeling choice in a received principle
variants: the principle can come from finance, statistics, or common practice
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the decision must follow from the principle; this paragraph is the bridge to Assumption 1 and should not be quoted as a proof

units.source_excerpt: Considering the background information and restricted conditions identified in the problem statement, we need to solve the following problems:
units.function: Credit the problem statement, then announce the task list that the rest of the paper answers.
units.reusable_pattern: A lead sentence crediting the problem, a colon, then one bullet per required output.
reusable_elements: stable function: turn the problem into an ordered list of outputs
variants: the bullets here mix imperatives with one gerund, which is kept as printed
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: every bullet must be answered by a later section; do not add a task the paper does not attempt

features.quantitative_role: the first bullet carries the dates and the 1000 dollars

units.source_excerpt: The flow chart of our idea is shown in Figure 1.
units.function: Hand the work plan to a figure in one sentence instead of narrating it.
units.reusable_pattern: One sentence pointing to the figure that carries the plan.
reusable_elements: stable function: let a figure carry the overview
variants: the sentence can name what the figure shows
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: use only when the figure really does show the plan; do not point to a figure and also repeat its whole content

units.source_excerpt: Assumption 1: Investor who will use this strategy is a risk-seeker who willing to take arbitrary risk for the sake of return. Justification: As explained in Section 1.1: strategies with different risks are not comparable.
units.function: State each assumption and follow it at once with a justification, four times.
units.reusable_pattern: Assumption N, the assumption, then Justification, the reason, and the reason may point back to an earlier section.
reusable_elements: stable function: never leave an assumption unsupported
variants: the justification can cite an earlier section, as the first one cites 1.1, or stand alone
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the justification must give a reason, not restate the assumption; keep all four pairs, do not collapse them

units.source_excerpt: Bull Market: A market with a long-term upward price trend. The overall trend is upward, with some declines, but one wave higher than the other.
units.function: Define a term with a colon, a one-line definition, then one sentence of character.
units.reusable_pattern: Term, colon, short definition, then a sentence that gives the texture.
reusable_elements: stable function: fix the meaning of a word before it is used
variants: some terms add a second sentence, some stop at one
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: define only terms the paper uses in a special sense; do not define ordinary words

units.source_excerpt: The key mathematical notations used in this paper are listed in Table 1.
units.function: Point to the notation table in one sentence instead of glossing every symbol in prose.
units.reusable_pattern: One sentence naming the table that holds the symbols.
reusable_elements: stable function: move a long symbol list into a table
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the table must actually contain the symbols; note this paper numbers two different tables as Table 1

units.source_excerpt: Knowing the time series, find the asset price in the future. The formula is shown in equation 1.
units.function: Move from a known series to the unknown future price and then point to the equation.
units.reusable_pattern: State what is known, what is wanted, then 'the formula is shown in equation N'.
reusable_elements: stable function: introduce an equation as the answer to a stated need
variants: the pointer can be 'is shown in equation N' or 'is given in equation N'
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the equation must express the stated relationship; do not point to an equation that does something else

units.source_excerpt: so our study combines the linear time series forecasting algorithm ARIMA and the nonlinear forecasting algorithm LSTM neural network together for volatile asset price forecasting.
units.function: Justify combining two methods by the mixed nature of the market, using 'so'.
units.reusable_pattern: The market is neither purely linear nor purely nonlinear, so the study combines one method of each kind.
reusable_elements: stable function: motivate a hybrid model from the data's character
order: character of the data, so, combination
slots: data character, method A, method B
variants: the same motive reappears in the strengths section
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the combination must be motivated by a stated property of the data

units.source_excerpt: Where yt is the current value; the constant term; the autocorrelation coefficient; the error term; the coefficient of error term.
units.function: Gloss every symbol in an equation with a 'Where' sentence, one clause each.
units.reusable_pattern: 'Where', then symbol and its meaning, repeated for each symbol, separated by semicolons.
reusable_elements: stable function: make an equation readable without guessing
variants: the same frame glosses equation 3 on page 11
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: gloss every symbol that appears, and no symbol that does not

units.section: 4.2.2 LSTM Neural Network Nonlinear Prediction Model
units.source_excerpt: Looking at Figure 4 we can see that the work of LSTM can be divided into 3 main steps. Step 1: Decide what information can pass through the cell state.
units.function: Read a figure as a count of steps, then give each step as 'Step N: action'.
units.reusable_pattern: Looking at Figure N, the work divides into N steps, then Step 1, Step 2, Step 3, each an action.
reusable_elements: stable function: turn a diagram into an ordered procedure
variants: the genetic operators in section 6.2.3 use the same Step N frame
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the steps must match the figure; do not add a step the figure does not show

units.section: 5.1 Dynamic Programming to Determine the Trading Strategy Process
units.source_excerpt: By splitting the 5-year trading process and defining the relationship between trading states and states, we can solve the problem in a recursive manner.
units.function: Describe dynamic programming as splitting one long problem into daily pieces.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the long problem, the act of splitting, and the recursive consequence.
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 5.1, repeated in the conclusion
stable function: explain why a long horizon becomes tractable
variants: the conclusion says 'transform long-term investment problems into short-term ones'
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: state the split that is actually performed; here it is into days

units.source_excerpt: From Figure 8, we can see that the ARIMA model is not very accurate in predicting the price of Bitcoin. However, the ARIMA model is still able to capture the trend of bitcoin price changes well.
units.function: Read a figure as a weakness first, then concede with 'However' what it still does.
units.reusable_pattern: From Figure N, the weakness, then However, the remaining strength.
reusable_elements: stable function: report a result without over-claiming
order: figure, limitation, however, what remains
variants: section 4.3.2 drops the concession and states an improvement instead
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the concession must be visible in the figure; do not praise a model the figure contradicts

units.source_excerpt: Therefore, we can conclude that the LSTM model is able to capture the information of the non-linear part of the asset price relatively well.
units.function: Draw a conclusion from a figure with 'Therefore, we can conclude', and keep it qualified.
units.reusable_pattern: A figure observation, then Therefore, a qualified conclusion.
reusable_elements: stable function: mark a conclusion as drawn from the evidence
variants: the qualifier 'relatively well' keeps it short of certainty
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: keep the qualifier; do not upgrade 'relatively well' to 'exactly'

units.source_excerpt: firstly, we based on the ARIMA prediction results; secondly, we phase space reconstruct the original data; thirdly, use the data after reconstructing; fourthly, input the training set; finally, the results are summed.
units.function: Narrate a multi-stage method with firstly through finally, one stage per ordinal.
units.reusable_pattern: Firstly, secondly, thirdly, fourthly, finally, each a stage with its output.
reusable_elements: stable function: make a long procedure followable
order: five ordinals, each a stage
variants: the memorandum uses firstly, secondly, finally for three stages
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the ordinals must match the real stages; do not skip or renumber

features.quantitative_role: a delay of 1 and an order of 7

units.section: 4.4 Comparative Analysis of Model Forecasting Performance
units.source_excerpt: By observing the Table 1, it is not difficult to find that: the RMSE and MAPE of ARIMA-LSTM model are very close to 0. This is because ARIMA-LSTM combines the advantages of ARIMA model and LSTM model.
units.function: Read a table with 'it is not difficult to find', state the result, then give the reason with 'because'.
units.reusable_pattern: By observing Table N, the finding, then This is because, the reason.
reusable_elements: stable function: connect a table's numbers to the reason
variants: 'it is easy to find' on page 9 is the same move with a lighter phrase
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the reason must explain the finding; do not attach an unrelated cause

features.transition: By observing, it is not difficult to find, because

units.section: 4.4 Comparative Analysis of Model Forecasting Performance
units.source_excerpt: Therefore, in the part of investment strategy, we will make investment decisions based on the predict results of the ARIMA-LSTM model.
units.function: Hand the result of one section to the next section with 'Therefore, in the part of'.
units.reusable_pattern: Therefore, name the next part, then what will be done there with this result.
reusable_elements: stable function: make the join between chapters explicit
order: therefore, next part, carried result
variants: none other in this paper
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the next section must actually use the named result

units.source_excerpt: the final asset value on September 10, 2021 was $442,697.25, with a five-year total return of 44,169.70%, an extremely good result compared to bitcoins 7458.97% and golds 135.48% over the same period.
units.function: State the result, then compare it against the two assets over the same period.
units.reusable_pattern: The value, the return, then 'compared to' the two benchmarks.
reusable_elements: stable function: show the result beats the obvious alternatives
order: result, return, compared to, benchmarks
variants: the memorandum says 'much higher than the returns of bitcoin and gold' without numbers
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the benchmarks must be the real alternatives; note the printed percentage conflicts with the dollar value

units.source_excerpt: Gene1: Trading Portfolio Information. So, we set the trading strategy as a non-deterministic variable in our trading system, i.e., Gene1. In this paper, we choose the method shown in the table below to encode it.
units.function: Introduce each gene as a name, a role, and a pointer to its encoding table.
units.reusable_pattern: Gene N: name, then what it decides, then 'i.e.' the label, then the table.
reusable_elements: stable function: present an encoded choice as name, role, table
variants: Gene4 adds the stop-loss percentages in prose before its table
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the table must list the codes the prose describes

features.transition: i.e., shown in the table below

units.source_excerpt: For example, if Gene1=101, it means that we will trade on cash and bitcoin. It is easy to see that this table covers all possible combinations.
units.function: Decode one code as an example, then claim the table is exhaustive.
units.reusable_pattern: For example, one code and what it means, then a sentence saying the table covers all cases.
reusable_elements: stable function: make an encoding readable and claim it is complete
variants: only Gene1 spells out an example
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the exhaustiveness claim must be true of the table; here the eight rows do cover the three-bit cases

features.transition: For example, It is easy to see

units.source_excerpt: Although there are many methods to evaluate the goodness of trading strategy selection, in this paper only the yield is used as the fitness evaluation function since we only know the asset price in this problem.
units.function: Concede that many measures exist, then justify the single one by what the data allows.
units.reusable_pattern: Although many options exist, this paper uses only one, since the data supports only that one.
reusable_elements: stable function: justify a narrow choice by a data limit
variants: the weakness section later admits this single measure is a limitation
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the reason must be a real data limit; do not claim the choice is best when the paper says it is the only one available

units.source_excerpt: In the second and third columns of the table, there are some cells with no data in them because there were no transactions made for gold during the period.
units.function: Explain an empty cell instead of leaving it to be read as a missing result.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the empty place, then because, the real reason.
reusable_elements: stable function: stop an empty cell from being misread
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the reason must be true; here gold was not traded in those periods

units.section: 7 Effectiveness Evaluation of The Trading Strategy
units.source_excerpt: To prove that our strategy is optimal in both aspects, we try to change the strategy itself and change the market environment respectively.
units.function: Restate the two-part proof and assign one change to each part.
units.reusable_pattern: To prove the claim, change one thing for the first part and another for the second.
reusable_elements: stable function: tie each test to the claim it serves
order: to prove, test one, test two
variants: the summary announced the same two ways
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: each test must bear on the claim; do not add a test that answers a different question

units.source_excerpt: As you can see from the chart, we have been able to maintain a holding position during large market rallies and sell assets in time to hedge our risk during some minor fluctuations.
units.function: Read a regime chart as what the strategy did, in plain 'as you can see'.
units.reusable_pattern: As you can see from the chart, the behavior in that regime.
reusable_elements: stable function: turn a marked chart into a sentence
order: as you can see, behavior
variants: the bear and the oscillating readings drop the phrase and state the behavior directly
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: describe only behavior the chart shows

features.transition: As you can see from the chart

units.source_excerpt: the return of the original strategy is much higher than the return of the current strategy, so it can be justified that the article is now a more reasonable strategy.
units.function: Compare the two returns and close with 'so it can be justified'.
units.reusable_pattern: The original beats the changed one, so the original is justified.
reusable_elements: stable function: turn a comparison into a verdict
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the verdict can only be as strong as the comparison; note the printed 442% and 273% are not reconciled with the headline yield

units.source_excerpt: Many strategies have good rates of return under ideal conditions, but may have lower rates of return once transaction costs change.
units.function: Motivate the sensitivity test by the gap between an ideal result and a costly one.
units.reusable_pattern: Good under ideal conditions, but lower once costs change.
reusable_elements: stable function: justify testing sensitivity before showing it
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the test must then vary the named condition

units.source_excerpt: To see the impact of transaction costs on trading outcomes, we replaced the transaction costs with the following four scenarios.
units.function: Introduce a scenario table with 'to see the impact, we replaced X with the following N scenarios'.
units.reusable_pattern: Purpose, the replacement, the count, then the table.
reusable_elements: stable function: frame a sensitivity table
order: to see, replaced, scenarios, table
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the table must contain the stated scenarios

units.source_excerpt: We find that when the commission is reduced on only one asset, the transaction frequency of the asset with reduced transaction cost will increase.
units.function: Report a sensitivity result as 'we find that when X, Y'.
units.reusable_pattern: We find that, the condition, then the effect.
reusable_elements: stable function: state a conditional result from a scenario
variants: the later readings drop 'we find that' and start at 'when'
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: each reading must match one scenario; do not merge scenarios

units.source_excerpt: I am the developer of this investment strategy. There are a few things we would like to tell you about our models, strategies and results.
units.function: Open the letter in the first person singular, then shift to we.
units.reusable_pattern: I am the developer, then we would like to tell you, naming the topics.
reusable_elements: stable function: address the reader directly
variants: the letter is signed Lee, a personal name
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: this voice belongs to the letter only; the body of the paper stays in we

units.source_excerpt: It is worth noting that as an emerging asset, Bitcoin comes with a high level of risk along with a high level of reward.
units.function: Flag a risk with 'it is worth noting' before the caveat.
units.reusable_pattern: It is worth noting, the risk, stated as a balance of reward and risk.
reusable_elements: stable function: warn without abandoning the strategy
variants: a second caveat follows, that the strategy does not buy the exact low or sell the exact high
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: the caveat must be a real limitation of the strategy

units.source_excerpt: Finally, thank you for your interest in our strategies and we wish you all the best in life.
units.function: Close the letter with thanks and a wish, not with a result.
units.reusable_pattern: Finally, thanks, and a good wish.
reusable_elements: stable function: end a letter on a human note
prohibited_generalizations: boundary: this closing belongs to a letter; do not end an analytical section this way

units.source_excerpt: By combining the ARIMA model with the LSTM model, both linear and non-linear situations can be taken into account, allowing attention to be paid to both trend changes and volatility.
units.function: State a strength as a by-doing clause that names the benefit.

prohibited_generalizations: boundary: each strength must name the method; do not list a benefit with no source

units.source_excerpt: the time series analysis method only uses historical price data, without considering the causes of stock price movements, so it is generally an intuitive analysis and only makes short term predictions.

units.source_excerpt: First of all, we should not stand in the perspective of God to invest, and we need to predict the daily asset price. In short, we were sure that the strategy we proposed was reasonable and effective.

units.reusable_pattern: First of all, the stance the paper refuses, then the recap, then In short, the verdict.
